title: Prefill Staircase Scheduler and Fragment Reuse Protocol for Paged KV Cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Under mixed short-and-long conversational workloads we observe tail spikes in prefill latency and frequent KV slot churn that increases decode stalls. Goal: Implement a low-risk scheduling and allocation protocol that reduces prefill tail latency, increases fragment reuse, and avoids excessive eviction-induced decode stalls. The feature combines a staircase prefill scheduler that issues decoupled prefill waves (fast shallow prefill followed by slower deep prefill), a slot-staging pool to avoid immediate writebacks on hot fragments, and a fragment reuse protocol that tags salvageable fragments with rewarm credits for preferential reuse by kernel cohorts.
design_summary: 1) Staircase scheduler: split prefill into ordered waves (T0 fast window for first N tokens, T1 deep window for long sequences). Waves carry 'urgency' tags used by kernel cohort-selector to prefer low-latency kernels for T0. 2) Slot-staging pool: transient holding area for recently-prefilled fragments to defer eviction; maintains soft-residency credits decaying over time. 3) Fragment reuse protocol: fragments are scored using touch-frequency, last-prefill-age, and kernel-match score; high-score fragments get 'sticky' hints that bias future kernel placement and avoid forced writebacks. 4) Admission policy: small probabilistic admission for large fragments under pressure to prevent thrash. 5) Metrics & tracepoints: new tags for prefill-wave-id, fragment-score, and kernel-cohort to aid rollout diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >= 25% on mixed demo workload (chat+long-completion)
Decode stall rate (prefill-triggered) reduced by >= 40% in CI load tests
No >5% regression in aggregate throughput for batch workloads
Automated canary rollout with runtime-1.26 flagged and rollback path tested
All new tracepoints and dashboards available in console perf tab
risks_mitigation: Risk: Staircase waves could create burstiness if misconfigured -> Mitigation: conservative defaults (T0 <= 64 tokens) and token-smoothing backoff
Risk: Slot-staging increases memory pressure -> Mitigation: cap staging pool by occupancy ratio and priority-evict low-score fragments
Risk: Kernel cohort bias may reduce kernel diversity -> Mitigation: cohort exploration multiplier and periodic randomization
Risk: Incorrect scoring yields cold misses -> Mitigation: short A/B canary with telemetry comparison and automatic revert threshold
